title: Structured action probes for higher-entropy hypothesis disambiguation
question: At matched environment-compute cost, can a structured execution trace carry more information about the unknown program hypothesis than scalar output probes, without exposing target identity?
hypothesis: A single target-identity-blind activation-trace action will provide higher empirical model information gain per unit environment execution work than a single scalar output-row action on the registered finite-domain workload.

arms.name: scalar_row
arms.intervention: execute one selected input row and observe only the binary program output

arms.name: activation_trace
arms.intervention: execute one selected input row and observe the vector of non-input node activation bits from the instrumented CASM sandbox

endpoints.name: best_one_step_information_gain_per_work
endpoints.role: primary — maximum deterministic model-information gain in bits per expected environment work unit, averaged across tasks within seed and then across seeds

endpoints.name: best_one_step_information_gain_bits
endpoints.role: secondary — maximum deterministic information gain before cost normalization

endpoints.name: expected_remaining_candidate_count
endpoints.role: secondary — expected compatible hypothesis-set size after the selected one-step action

endpoints.name: signature_support_size
endpoints.role: secondary — number of distinct evidence signatures induced by the candidate set for the selected action

endpoints.name: candidate_pool_reduction_fraction
endpoints.role: secondary — normalized reduction in expected compatible candidate count

held_constant: G-CASM-010 generator and pinned external generator commit
same five seeds, M levels and 32 tasks per seed/M
same deterministic target selection and row-action domain
same train/evaluation structure and truth disjointness rules
leakage_rules: The action selector may use only the current compatible hypothesis set and public predicted evidence for each candidate/action pair.
The target identity and target index are not supplied to the selector.
The target's realized evidence is exposed only after the action is selected.
No held-out verifier rows are supplied as probe-selection labels.
No confirmatory result is used to tune the channel definitions, action set, or endpoint.

information_definition.prior: uniform over the current compatible candidate set
information_definition.deterministic_mutual_information_bits: H(E_a | H_t) in bits because each candidate deterministically predicts the action evidence

activation_trace.evidence: ordered binary activation vector for all non-input active nodes
activation_trace.environment_work: one exact graph execution plus one trace-read unit per returned activation bit
activation_trace.scope_note: This is an instrumented-sandbox channel measurement, not a claim that arbitrary black-box environments expose internal activations.

decision_rule.condition: Activation-trace primary utility exceeds scalar utility with a seed-level interval excluding zero.
decision_rule.licenses: evidence that the richer instrumented observation channel is more information-efficient than scalar observation on the registered workload.
decision_rule.does_not_license: learned autonomous probe selection, arbitrary-environment internal-state access, or multimodal capability.

decision_rule.condition: Activation-trace has higher raw information but no utility advantage after work normalization.
decision_rule.licenses: the channel carries more entropy but its observation cost offsets the gain.
the registered activation channel does not improve information efficiency on this workload.
decision_rule.does_not_license: impossibility of other structured evidence channels such as relational or counterfactual probes.

schedule.note: 015 is an exact finite-domain observation-channel ceiling; no learned optimization occurs in this experiment.
